correctness.rationale: For odd n, det(I+P)=2 and sum y_i=n-2sum x_i prove the missing cap is the inverse image of a full standard simplex, not merely a subset. The simplex vertices invert to all-half and the n maximum stable-set indicator vectors; therefore coordinate nonnegativity is automatic and the volume equals 1/(2n!). The trace of the kernel 1_{u+v<=1} gives the full fractional-cycle volume via a complete Sturm-Liouville eigenbasis and the exact Euler/beta identity. Uniform cap coordinates are Dirichlet, giving alternating signed cumulative exponential increments and a functional triangular-array CLT after random-total normalization. The covariance eigenbasis of the antiperiodic Laplacian yields the displayed spectral law, Laplace transform and limits. Dirichlet second moments give the exact finite mean. Standalone reproducible code checks n=5,7,11,19 simplex inverses and n=5 to 501 sampled means; simulations do not substitute for infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: Statement-level comparison: the first anchor computes fractional stable-set circuit directions and diameter, while the second proves the integral convex-hull facet; neither gives conditional Euclidean cap measures. Two highly relevant published full result texts treat, respectively, the odd-cycle minimum enclosing ball and maximum-volume inscribed ellipsoid; their extremal-radius/contact statements do not imply the Dirichlet cap distribution, Brownian process limit or hyperbolic-secant law. The closest own geometry claim concerns unconditional covariance of volume-uniform fractional-cycle points and cannot recover a law conditional on a superfactorially small simplex. Exact initial probability and classical stochastic/spectral tools alone are not claimed as novelty. Residual risk: a differently named conditional-simplex/Brownian-functional result might imply the law.

value.rationale: Odd-hole inequalities are canonical integrality corrections for stable-set relaxations. The precise *conditional Euclidean geometry* of the excluded volume is a natural, informative question: an asymptotically superfactorially rare integrality violation nonetheless occupies macroscopic Euclidean radii about the exceptional half-integral vertex. The nondegenerate antiperiodic Brownian limit, exact hyperbolic-secant Laplace law and finite conditional mean give a genuine distributional characterization beyond a routine facet or small-volume calculation. This is not a known-table recomputation and is not implied by the nearest extremal sphere/ellipsoid invariants. The restriction to odd cycles is structurally motivated by invertibility of I+P and the unique odd-cycle inequality.
